name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
title: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
answer: Finding patterns in lived experience is a qualitative and mixed methods research activity. It looks for recurring themes, meanings, tensions, and narrative arcs in interviews, diaries, focus groups, observation notes, open survey responses, and other accounts. The aim is not to reduce experience to a single score but to build an interpretable account of how people describe events, relationships, and feelings. Mixed methods work connects those patterns to counts, measures, or contextual variables when the design calls for it. This topic sits in qualitative analysis and mixed methods, part of The AI Researcher.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Finding patterns in lived experience is a qualitative and mixed methods research activity. It looks for recurring themes, meanings, tensions, and narrative arcs in interviews, diaries, focus groups, observation notes, open survey responses, and other accounts. The aim is not to reduce experience to a single score but to build an interpretable account of how people describe events, relationships, and feelings. Mixed methods work connects those patterns to counts, measures, or contextual variables when the design calls for it. This topic sits in qualitative analysis and mixed methods, part of The AI Researcher.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on transcripts, field notes, audio, video, images, and documents, plus the software used to store, transcribe, code, and retrieve them. Common platforms include NVivo, ATLAS.ti, MAXQDA, Dedoose, Taguette, and QualCoder, alongside general tools such as spreadsheets, Python, R, and qualitative data analysis libraries. AI assistance may come from speech to text, large language models, embeddings, topic models, and clustering routines, run either in the cloud or on local machines. Secure storage, access controls, versioning, and backup matter because qualitative material often contains identifiable detail. The choice of infrastructure shapes what can be searched, compared, and audited later.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Researchers typically begin with close reading and open coding, then group codes into candidate themes or patterns. They may use inductive approaches such as grounded theory or thematic analysis, or deductive frameworks drawn from prior literature. Constant comparison, memo writing, negative case analysis, and reflexive journaling help test whether a pattern holds across participants and contexts. AI can speed up transcription, summarization, semantic search, topic modeling, and clustering, but the resulting candidates still need human interpretation and checking against the source. In mixed methods designs, joint displays and integration matrices show how qualitative patterns align with or complicate quantitative findings.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Ethical practice centers on informed consent, privacy, anonymization, and the right of participants and communities to understand how their accounts are used. Re-identification risk, secondary use, data sovereignty, and community agreements are part of the review, along with institutional ethics approval and applicable data protection rules. Provenance matters, so this site links to the original paper rather than a search tool, and its library currently holds 135 research papers and 12646 claims extracted from research works. Audit trails, codebooks, model documentation, and clear notes on where AI assisted help others inspect the path from raw account to reported pattern. Bias, exclusion, and the risk of flattening minority experience are treated as analytic concerns, not only technical ones.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward more transparent AI-assisted coding, better provenance for model outputs, and tighter integration of qualitative and quantitative evidence. Researchers are testing retrieval augmented generation, local models, and participatory design to keep interpretation closer to the people who provided the accounts. Evaluation is shifting from simple agreement scores toward usefulness, traceability, and whether a pattern changes a decision or a theory. Mixed methods teams are likely to spend more effort on shared data models, reusable codebooks, and reporting standards that make AI assistance visible. The unresolved question is how to gain scale without losing the particularity that makes lived experience worth studying.
